hook: The anomaly here is a belief: that the world ends on March 5th, 2019, and that killing yourself before then is the right choice. The page deals with mass suicide head-on, through containment procedures, samples of infected media and a dated timeline. Read the parts in order and watch how each one shifts as the date gets closer.
whyItMatters: It is a K-class scenario with no monster at its center, only an idea, and the Foundation's own forecast for the date never rises above the ordinary baseline. The article turns the standard document layout into a countdown, so the structure of the page tells as much of the story as any single line. A footnote marks the first broadcast as carrying Fifth Church influence, which places it near that thread of the setting.
thingsToNotice:
The procedures at the top are not one set but a stack of successive versions, matching the revision entries in the timeline. Between versions the countermeme distribution list drops the O5 Council, the GOC and the WHO, later versions add grief counseling, suicide capsules and abandon-in-place orders, and the opening paragraph is the final state: nobody susceptible is left, so the meme is declared neutralized. The countermeme itself never reaches the public, because RAISA reports it could not be put into carrier media in the field.

Once the project flees to a cabin near Bishop, the log turns into first-person notes, project heads die one after another, and the automatic line of succession makes a junior researcher O5-6. By then even uninfected staff are killing themselves, treating the collapse itself as proof of the prophecy. The entry for March 5th is blank, and the one for the next day says only that the weather is beautiful, written by someone who is apparently among the very few still alive.
